Comment: M7 extraction pipeline (D-035, docs/architecture/reviews/m7-extraction-design/claude-reconciliation-final-design.md, GATE 9.2/9.3). RunTextract/RunDeterministicParser/RunBedrock are real Task states now (items 4/5/6). ValidateSchema/CompareExtractors/PersistExtractedFields/MarkPendingConfirmation/CompleteRun (item 7, ExtractionValidationTaskHandler) are still placeholders/stubs. This file documents the intended shape; it MUST NOT be applied via a real aws_sfn_state_machine resource until item 7's Lambda exists (a Task referencing a non-existent function ARN fails terraform apply, not just runtime) - see infra/modules/extraction-workflow/ (parameterized by Lambda ARN variables, deliberately not called from infra/main.tf yet) and NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md for wiring status.

RunTextract.Comment: The only real Task state for this phase (design §2, rodada 5 correction: no separate DetectDocumentType state - classification happens INSIDE this single TextractTaskHandler invocation, per §1.2). Sequence inside the handler: classify -> OCR kill switch -> reserve AI_CALL quota -> StartDocumentTextDetection -> persist TextractJob, then return (no SendTaskSuccess here - the execution stays parked on taskToken until a LATER, separate SQS-triggered COMPLETE_OCR invocation resolves it via SendTaskSuccess/Failure).

Catch.Comment: UnsupportedDocumentType (classifier), OcrDisabled (kill switch), TextractUnsupportedDocument/TextractPartialFailure/TextractJobPersistenceFailed (Textract-time failures), and any timeout/unclassified error - ALL fall through to the deterministic parser, never straight to MarkPendingConfirmation (design §1.2 rodada-3 correction).

RunDeterministicParser.Comment: PdfParserTaskHandler (item 5, D-035 SS1.3) - real Lambda now. Runs a deterministic parser over the OCR artifact (when present) to produce candidate field values, per implementation-blueprint.md SS12.5. A RunTextract failure above (ocrFailure present) still reaches this state and must run degraded (no OCR text, returns no candidates rather than a fabricated file-metadata heuristic - see NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md pending decision) - never skipped. Item 6 correction: ResultSelector+OutputPath now unwrap the raw arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke response (which wraps the handler's real return value under Payload/ExecutedVersion/StatusCode) down to the handler's own RunDeterministicParserOutput shape, so every state from here on (NeedsBedrock/CheckAiKillSwitch/RunBedrock) reads $.needsBedrock/$.aiExtractionEnabled/$.artifact directly - RunBedrock's own Payload.$: "$" therefore sends RunBedrockExtractionInput (mirroring RunDeterministicParserOutput exactly, see run-bedrock-extraction.ts) straight to BedrockExtractionTaskHandler, unwrapped. ValidateSchema (item 7, still a stub) will need its own OutputPath once RunBedrock's real output shape is finalized together with item 7.

Catch.Comment: The ONE failure that goes straight to MarkPendingConfirmation without trying Bedrock - a RunDeterministicParser failure itself, per design §1.2. ResultPath here means the Catch payload is NOT run through ResultSelector/OutputPath above (those only apply to a successful Task result), so $ keeps its pre-Task shape (either completeOcr's re-attached context, or the original execution input) with .parserFailure appended - the same shape MarkPendingConfirmation already expected before this state existed for real.

NeedsBedrock.Comment: Real condition (item 6) - $.needsBedrock is now a top-level field of RunDeterministicParser's unwrapped output (see that state's ResultSelector/OutputPath above).

CheckAiKillSwitch.Comment: AI_EXTRACTION kill switch gate before any paid Bedrock call, fail-closed per design §1.5 - $.aiExtractionEnabled was read once by RunDeterministicParser (AppConfig call) and is re-checked again, defense in depth, inside BedrockExtractionTaskHandler itself (run-bedrock-extraction.ts) before it spends the quota reservation.

RunBedrock.Comment: BedrockExtractionTaskHandler (item 6, D-035 SS1.9/SS1.11) - real Lambda now. Converse API, prompt isolation (versioned immutable system message, untrusted user block, closed submit_extraction tool schema with forced tool choice, temperature 0, token limit), BedrockExtractionRequest carries only textArtifact (never raw OCR text - the adapter resolves it internally via OcrArtifactStore.get()), AI_CALL quota reserved (idempotent per runId|BEDROCK, same pattern as RunTextract's runId|TEXTRACT) before the call. Input is RunDeterministicParser's unwrapped output directly (Payload.$: "$" - see that state's comment); same invoke shape as RunDeterministicParser (no waitForTaskToken), so its own output needs the identical unwrap for whatever consumes it next (item 7, not yet implemented - left as a plain lambda:invoke wrapper here since ValidateSchema is still a stub).

Catch.Comment: A RunBedrock failure never re-fabricates a value and never blocks the run - it still proceeds to ValidateSchema/CompareExtractors with only the deterministic candidates available, exactly like the ocrFailure/parserFailure Catches above degrade gracefully rather than dead-ending the execution.

ValidateSchema.Comment: STUB - first of 4 distinct Task states from ExtractionValidationTaskHandler (item 7, not yet implemented), per design §2's closing paragraph (kept as separate states for per-stage audit/Catch, overhead is negligible next to Textract/Bedrock).

CompareExtractors.Comment: STUB - compares deterministic vs. Bedrock candidates (when both ran), decides ExtractedFieldState (CONFIRMED/PENDING_CONFIRMATION/DISAGREEMENT) per data-model.md.

MarkPendingConfirmation.Comment: STUB - reached either from a RunDeterministicParser failure (no usable candidate at all) or from the normal path when a field needs human confirmation. Also the state responsible (per design §3) for deleting the transient OCR artifact when the run does NOT proceed to CompleteRun.

CompleteRun.Comment: STUB - terminal success state. Deletes the transient OCR artifact (design §3: the only point in the system that knows for certain no later state will read it) and marks ExtractionRun COMPLETED.
